premise: A cartographer hired to map a valley that refuses to stay the same shape must deliver a final map before the funding review.
tone: wry literary fabulism with a dry institutional edge — a landscape that will not hold still, told in the plain register of fieldwork notebooks and grant paperwork; melancholy and quiet humour, no horror, no spectacle, the strangeness always measured before it is felt

title: What the Stones Fix

gate_summary.note: stress profile (9-10 beats in a 300-550 band, tolerance 0). The outline-vs-length tension the fixture was built to force did not materialise: all six drafts sat inside the band with every beat present. The one rejection (ch3 attempt 1) was on prose (1 major, 1 minor). The third attempt, the literal-replacement sheet and patch_then_halt were therefore not exercised on this run either.

summaries_over_cap.note: measured after it had gone into chapter 3's packet; left as written per SKILL.md (trim the next, never truncate one already written). ch01 119, ch03 120.

faulted a sentence that reproduces bible/timeline.md Chapter 3 and the audited outline beat 10 under R4

orchestrator_lessons: Count a summary with the script BEFORE it goes into the next packet, not beside the dispatch. ch02's went out at 133 words against 120 because the check and the dispatch were issued in the same reply.
Putting a disputed finding back to the critic with the canon it missed worked twice and kept the score the critic's rather than the orchestrator's; both times the critic withdrew or downgraded.
When the outline audit sends beats back for rewriting, re-audit the rewritten beats; here the rewritten beat 10 was not re-audited and a science critic later faulted the sentence built from it.
